message.content:
**Quick note:**  
`docker start <container>` is used to **start an existing container**, *not* to start the Docker daemon/service itself.  
To get the Docker engine running on Windows you need to start the Docker service (or launch Docker Desktop). Below are the most common ways to do this:

---

### 1️⃣ Start Docker Desktop (GUI)

If you have Docker Desktop installed (the standard way to run Docker on Windows):

1. Press **Win + S** → type “Docker Desktop” → click the app icon.  
2. Docker Desktop will launch and automatically start the Docker Engine in the background.  
3. Once the whale icon turns blue (or shows “Docker Desktop is running”), you’re ready to use Docker.

> **Tip:** You can also pin Docker Desktop to the taskbar for quick access.

---

### 2️⃣ Start the Docker Service via PowerShell

If you prefer a command‑line approach or are working on a headless machine:

```powershell
# Run PowerShell as Administrator
Start-Service -Name Docker
```

Or, using the classic `net` command:

```cmd
net start com.docker.service
```

> **What happens?**  
> These commands start the Windows service named `com.docker.service`, which runs the Docker Engine (`dockerd.exe`). Once the service status changes to “Running”, you can immediately issue Docker CLI commands.

---

### 3️⃣ Verify Docker is Running

After starting the service, confirm everything is up:

```bash
docker version
```

You should see output similar to:

```
Client:
 Version:           24.x.x
 API version:       1.41
 Go version:        go1.xx
 Git commit:        abcdefg
 Built:             Mon Jul 8 12:34:56 2026
 OS/Arch:           windows/amd64
 Experimental:      false

Server:
 Engine:
  Version:          24.x.x
  API version:      1.41 (minimum version 1.12)
  Go version:       go1.xx
  Git commit:       hijklmn
  Built:            Mon Jul 8 12:34:56 2026
  OS/Arch:          linux/amd64
  Experimental:     false
```

If you see the “Server” section, Docker is fully operational.

---

### 4️⃣ Optional: Set Docker to Auto‑Start

If you want Docker to start automatically when you log in:

```powershell
Set-Service -Name Docker -StartupType Automatic
```

Now the Docker service will start at boot without manual intervention.

---

#### Common Pitfalls & Fixes

| Symptom | Likely Cause | Quick Fix |
|---------|--------------|-----------|
| `docker: Cannot connect to the Docker daemon at unix:///var/run/docker.sock. Is the docker daemon running?` | Service isn’t running | Run `Start-Service Docker` (PowerShell) or launch Docker Desktop |
| `docker: Error response from daemon: client is newer than server` | Client/Server mismatch | Update Docker Desktop or Docker Engine to the same major/minor version |
| `docker: command not found` | Docker CLI not in PATH | Ensure Docker Desktop’s installation path is added to your system’s PATH variable |

---

### Bottom Line

- **Use `docker start <container>` only after Docker is already running.**  
- To start Docker itself, either launch Docker Desktop or run `Start-Service Docker` in PowerShell.  

Let me know if you hit any errors or need help configuring Docker to start automatically!
